To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children with DS are less exposed to literacy in their homes than typically developing children, that they have less interest in reading and that their literacy skills are lower than those of their typically developing peers.

The home literacy environment and the child's interest in reading are important predictors of the child's emergent literacy skills, and that these variables are more strongly related to each other than to the child's developmental age.
